text:
incident-bot: PAGER: p99 tail latency breach on /streaming/generate (rwd-contbatch pool). p95=420ms p99=1.6s, streaming stalls observed. SLOs tripped. Paging #eng-oncall :rotating_light:

jamie: oncall here, grabbing it. any customer-facing errors?

priya: console shows increased queue depth on contbatch scheduler and a spike in pack sizes from some tenants. looks like mixed-seqlen amplification.

kevin: can you paste the query?

priya: `SELECT bin(1m), p50, p95, p99 FROM latency WHERE path='/streaming/generate' AND pool='rwd-contbatch'` -> last 10m: p95 420ms -> 480ms -> 650ms, p99 900ms -> 1.2s -> 1.6s.

priya: also seeing a tail of stalled streams with `streaming.wait_ms > 2000` and `batch_size > 20` host=usw2-gpu-12.

jamie: hypothesis: continuous batching scheduler is packing very large heterogeneous batches (mixed seq lengths) causing KV paging/prefetch stalls and blocking streaming preemptions.

sasha: +1. Recent traffic shows a tenant sending many long sequences, pads causing others to wait. fairness weight seems lower for streaming lanes.

lina: quick mitigation idea: reduce max_batch_size for contbatch pool and enable per-stream preemption (streaming_preempt=true) to favor low-latency streams.

kevin: can we patch config live? runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/contbatch-tail

jamie: let's do quick mitigations in this order: 1) set max_batch_size=8 for contbatch, 2) enable streaming_preempt, 3) route heavy tenants to ded. If step1 reduces p99 we hold.

marc: tagging customer-impact team to confirm if any API errors: @support-team.

priya: running patch now -> `POST /admin/pools/rwd-contbatch/config {"max_batch_size":8}` -> 200 OK.

incident-bot: deploy-bot: config update applied to pool rwd-contbatch (version v2026-11-03-08).

priya: enabling streaming preempt -> `PATCH /admin/pools/rwd-contbatch {"streaming_preempt":true}` -> applied.

jamie: monitoring p95/p99...

(priya updates dashboard)

priya: 3m after changes: p95 down to 350ms, p99 down to 700ms. streaming.wait_ms tail decreased. visible reduction in pack sizes >20.

kevin: good. any customers reporting degraded throughput?

marc: support says 2 customers saw slower throughput on bulk endpoints but no 5xxs. they were moved to dedicated pools as part of mitigation routing.

sasha: we should also consider a scheduler fairness tweak: increase streaming queue weight and add tenant-level max_pack_size to prevent noisy neighbors.

jamie: agree. immediate: schedule a canary change to add tenant max_pack_size=12 and bump streaming_queue_weight +20%.

lina: will open a PR for the scheduler change and run canary in prod in low-traffic region.

priya: quick root-cause notes: mixed-seqlen tenant(s) caused large batches, padding amplified compute time, batch scheduling didn't preempt streaming quickly enough -> queue head-of-line blocking -> p99 spikes. KV cache hotlines increased memory churn, contributing to stalls.

jamie: action items: 1) Marc to run postmortem and owner for follow-up (scheduler fairness + tenant protections). 2) Priya to add automated alert that triggers when avg batch_size>16 and streaming.wait_ms>500. 3) Lina to PR scheduler weight change + canary. 4) Kevin to validate routing playbook for heavy tenants.

marc: taking postmortem. assigning follow-ups in tracker. timeline will include when config patch applied and traffic impact.

lina: can we keep streaming_preempt enabled? it helped a lot.

jamie: keep it on for now. we'll include in rollback criteria.

priya: last check: p99 stabilizing ~650ms, no new pages in last 8m. marking incident as mitigated.

incident-bot: Incident mitigated by oncall team. create follow-up ticket for postmortem. :white_check_mark:

kevin: thanks all — nice quick mitigation.

marc: will draft the postmortem and include suggested long-term fixes: tenant-level pack limits, scheduler preemption primitives, adaptive batch-size cap based on seqlen distribution.

jamie: closing loop. if anything flips back, re-open paging. otherwise we handle follow-ups asynchronously. :thumbsup:
